papers.title: Integrative single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses identify LMX1B as a tumor suppressor orchestrating the GDF15-ATP4B axis in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is characterized by profound inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity and extensive tumor microenvironment (TME) remodeling, yet the spatially resolved cellular programs and intercellular communication networks orchestrating malignant progression remain poorly defined. LMX1B, a LIM homeodomain transcription factor essential for kidney morphogenesis, has not been previously investigated in renal carcinogenesis.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to map the cellular programs and intercellular communication networks driving renal cell carcinoma progression. The authors identify the transcription factor LMX1B as a tumor suppressor that regulates a GDF15-ATP4B signaling axis in the tumor microenvironment. The work nominates LMX1B as a previously unrecognized player in renal carcinogenesis.

papers.title: Uninflamed colonic tissue harbors humoral activity linked to anti-TNF therapy non-response in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: Anti-TNF therapy is central for treating ulcerative colitis, yet ∼40% are primary non-responders. To find pre-treatment signatures distinguishing anti-TNF non-responders from responders, we did serum cytokine profiling and laser microdissection transcriptomics on paired uninflamed and inflamed colonic epithelium and lamina propria from patients matched at baseline but differing in endoscopic outcome. Although inflammation drove more epithelial changes, the signatures separating non-responders from responders were found in uninflamed lamina propria, with elevated cell-cycle genes and a co-expre
papers.summary: This study profiled serum cytokines and performed laser-microdissection transcriptomics on paired inflamed and uninflamed colonic tissue from ulcerative colitis patients who either responded or did not respond to anti-TNF therapy. Surprisingly, the transcriptional signatures that distinguished non-responders from responders were found in uninflamed lamina propria rather than inflamed tissue, with elevated cell-cycle genes and a co-expression module suggesting local humoral activity. These pre-treatment features in apparently healthy tissue may help predict anti-TNF non-response.

papers.title: STCGCar: Graph Contrastive Learning with Reliable Augmentation for Spatial Transcriptomics Clustering.
papers.abstract: Accurately identifying spatial domains based on spatial transcriptomics (ST) data can greatly promote our understanding of cellular composition and tissue organization. While graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown significant advancements in spatial clustering, they tend to be insensitive to noisy edges, leading to intersections among identified spatial domains. Here, we introduce a GNN-based ST Clustering framework, called STCGCar, utilizing a Graph Contrastive learning model with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction strategies. The framework begins by creating an enhanced view thr
papers.summary: STCGCar is a graph neural network framework that uses graph contrastive learning with reliable augmentation and redundancy reduction to cluster spatial transcriptomics data into spatial domains. It addresses the tendency of existing GNN methods to be insensitive to noisy edges, which causes spatial domains to overlap. The approach aims to improve the accuracy of identifying tissue organization and cellular composition from spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Disentangling the cellular composition of FLCN-mutated tumors in Birt-Hogg-Dubé Syndrome by spatial transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Birt-Hogg-Dubé (BHD) syndrome is a hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome caused by pathogenic variants in the folliculin (FLCN) gene and is associated with an increased risk of multifocal renal tumors. FLCN-mutated tumors (FMTs) often exhibit morphological heterogeneity with mixed morphological features resembling renal oncocytoma (RO) and chromophobe renal cell carcinoma (chRCC), yet the molecular basis underlying the heterogeneous morphologic features and the morphologic-genomic correlations remain poorly defined. In our prior work, we identified mutually exclusive expressions of L1 cell
papers.journal: Modern pathology : an official journal of the United States and Canadian Academy of Pathology, Inc
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics to dissect the cellular composition of FLCN-mutated renal tumors in Birt-Hogg-Dubé syndrome, which often show mixed features resembling oncocytoma and chromophobe RCC. The authors link distinct cell populations and expression patterns to the tumors' morphological heterogeneity, providing a molecular basis for the morphologic-genomic correlations.

papers.title: A Molecularly Anchored Spatial Transcriptomic Framework for Precise CA1-Subiculum Parcellation and Region-Resolved Analysis in Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: The precise molecular delineation of the interface between the Subiculum (Sub) and cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) is a challenge in hippocampal research, as conventional cytoarchitectural boundaries are often ambiguous and limit reproducible regional annotation. Here, we developed a molecularly anchored spatial transcriptomic framework to define CA1-Sub regional identities using high-definition spatial transcriptomics (Stereo-seq) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) references.
papers.summary: This study introduces a molecularly anchored spatial transcriptomic framework that uses Stereo-seq and snRNA-seq to precisely define the boundary between the CA1 and Subiculum regions of the hippocampus, overcoming the ambiguity of traditional cytoarchitectural boundaries. The framework enables reproducible region-resolved analysis in Alzheimer's disease research.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics reveals OAT-associated arginine-proline metabolic remodeling in Paraquat-induced Parkinsonian and depression-like phenotypes.
papers.abstract: Paraquat (PQ) is a highly toxic bipyridyl herbicide that remains in agricultural use in some regions despite bans or severe restrictions elsewhere and is also widely used as a model toxicant for investigating environmentally induced neurodegeneration. However, the spatial metabolic alterations associated with PQ-induced neurobehavioral impairment remain incompletely understood. In this study, we performed AFADESI-MSI-based spatial metabolomic profiling and Visium spatial transcriptomic profiling on PQ-exposed mouse brains, and integrated these analyses with targeted metabolite assays, molecula
papers.summary: This study integrates spatial metabolomics (AFADESI-MSI) and spatial transcriptomics (Visium) to map metabolic and gene expression changes in mouse brains exposed to the herbicide paraquat, a model toxicant for Parkinson's disease. The authors identify OAT-associated remodeling of arginine-proline metabolism as a key feature linked to Parkinsonian and depression-like behavioral phenotypes. The work links spatially resolved metabolic dysregulation to neurobehavioral outcomes in an environmental neurotoxicity model.

papers.title: Machine learning-based identification of core regulatory targets in 1-nitropyrene-induced placental trophoblast dysfunction and FGR.
papers.abstract: 1-NP (1-Nitropyrene), a nitrated polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derived from diesel combustion, is a widespread environmental pollutant with potential reproductive toxicity. However, its role in FGR (fetal growth restriction) and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Our in vivo results revealed that 1-NP exposure leads to FGR and placental damage in mice, marked by reduced fetal and placental weights, and altered labyrinthine morphology. Integration of scRNA-seq (single-cell RNA sequencing) and bulk RNA-seq data using the Scissor algorithm identified EVTs (extravillous trophoblasts) as t
papers.summary: This study shows that exposure to 1-nitropyrene, a diesel-derived pollutant, causes fetal growth restriction and placental damage in mice. By combining single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing with a machine learning algorithm, the authors pinpoint extravillous trophoblasts as the key cell type affected and identify core regulatory targets underlying the dysfunction.

papers.title: Cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics in adult Drosophila neurons.
papers.abstract: The Drosophila adult central brain contains 240 circadian neurons, of which there are more than 25 different neuron subtypes based on connectomic data. Recent single-cell RNA-seq characterization of these neurons "around the clock" also indicates a similar number of molecular subtypes of circadian neurons, but other conclusions from these transcriptomic studies warranted verifying and extending with other approaches. To address these limitations, we used three complementary approaches: 1) We used a genetic multiplexing strategy to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons from multiple t
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: This study uses genetic multiplexing to profile the transcriptomes of circadian neurons in the adult Drosophila brain, revealing cell-type-specific circadian and light-responsive transcriptional dynamics. It provides a higher-resolution view of how distinct neuron subtypes within the circadian network regulate gene expression across the day and in response to light.

papers.title: Multi-omics and experimental validation identify RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Kidney Renal Clear Cell Carcinoma (KIRC) is characterized by marked molecular heterogeneity and metabolic reprogramming, underscoring the need for reliable biomarkers for prognostic assessment and individualized treatment. RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor has been implicated in cell adhesion and differentiation, but its role in KIRC remains unclear. In this study, we systematically evaluated the expression pattern, prognostic significance, genomic associations, biological function, and therapeutic relevance of RAPGEF2 in KIRC through integrated multi-omics analyses and experimenta
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with experimental validation to show that RAPGEF2, a guanine nucleotide exchange factor, is downregulated in clear cell renal cell carcinoma and that higher expression is associated with better patient prognosis. The authors characterize its genomic associations, biological functions, and potential therapeutic relevance, proposing RAPGEF2 as a protective prognostic biomarker for this cancer.

papers.title: TRPV1-STAT3 signaling as a driver of lethal pathology during pneumococcal nose-to-brain invasion.
papers.abstract: Nose-to-brain infection represents a non-hematogenous route by which pathogens invade the central nervous system via neural pathways. The olfactory and trigeminal systems are implicated in this process, but the molecular mechanisms underlying lethal pathology remain incompletely understood. We hypothesized that trigeminal TRPV1 and downstream STAT3 signaling contribute to disease progression during pneumococcal nose-to-brain infection. A murine intranasal infection model using Streptococcus pneumoniae was established with methimazole-induced olfactory epithelial damage and/or resiniferatoxin-m
papers.summary: This study investigates how Streptococcus pneumoniae invades the brain via the nose, focusing on the trigeminal nerve pathway. The authors show that TRPV1 and downstream STAT3 signaling drive lethal pathology during this nose-to-brain infection, suggesting these molecules as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Spatial analysis reveals the evolving organization of IDH-mutant glioma.
papers.abstract: Adult diffuse gliomas are composed of malignant cell states interwoven with the non-malignant brain microenvironment. Here, we combine spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas to define organizational principles across histological grades. In low-grade tumors, spatial organization is shaped by underlying brain anatomy. We identify a functional white-gray matter junction that restricts cortical invasion and is associated with marked changes in tumor composition and cellular phenotypes. This junction is preferentially traversed by oligodendr
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomics and spatial proteomics to map how IDH-mutant gliomas organize across histological grades. In low-grade tumors, organization follows brain anatomy, with a white-gray matter junction that limits cortical invasion and is preferentially crossed by oligodendroglioma cells. The work reveals how tumor cell states and the non-malignant microenvironment evolve together in space.

papers.title: Multi-modal analysis of vascular remodelling in human obliterative bronchiolitis after lung transplantation.
papers.abstract: Chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) is the leading cause of late morbidity and mortality after lung transplantation. Bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome (BOS), a major CLAD phenotype, is characterized by obliterative bronchiolitis (OB). While microvascular perturbations are described in BOS, their cellular and molecular characteristics remain unclear. Intact human CLAD lungs (n=3) underwent hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) for three-dimensional vascular mapping. In OB-affected airways vs. controls (n=4 each), endothelial subtypes were characterized by multiplex immunofluores
papers.journal: American journal of transplantation : official journal of the American Society of Transplantation and the American Society of Transplant Surgeons
papers.summary: This study uses hierarchical phase-contrast tomography (HiP-CT) to map the three-dimensional vasculature of intact human lungs with obliterative bronchiolitis (OB) after lung transplantation, combined with multiplex immunofluorescence to characterize endothelial subtypes in affected airways versus controls. The work reveals microvascular perturbations associated with chronic lung allograft dysfunction, providing cellular and molecular detail on vascular remodelling in this condition.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics reveals atorvastatin modulates the tumor microenvironment to suppress breast cancer liver metastatic outgrowth.
papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer remains incurable, underscoring the need for novel therapeutic strategies. Epidemiological and preclinical evidence suggests statins suppress metastatic outgrowth, however the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We employed high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (ST) to explore the cellular composition and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in the metastatic microenvironment following atorvastatin treatment. Formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded breast cancer liver metastases from control and atorvastatin-treated mice were analyzed by Nanostring CosMx Spatial Molecul
papers.summary: Using high-resolution spatial transcriptomics (Nanostring CosMx) on breast cancer liver metastases in mice, this study shows that atorvastatin remodels the metastatic tumor microenvironment and alters gene expression to suppress metastatic outgrowth. The work provides mechanistic insight into how statins may limit breast cancer progression beyond their cholesterol-lowering effects.

papers.title: Disentangling covariate effects on single-cell-resolved epigenomes with DeepDive.
papers.abstract: Understanding the effects of individual biological factors from single-cell-resolved epigenomic data is hindered by multicollinearity, particularly in human cohorts. We introduce DeepDive, a deep-learning framework designed to systematically disentangle known and unknown sources of variation in single-nucleus ATAC-seq data. DeepDive accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms state-of-the-art methods with incomplete covariate information, and robustly recovers true biological signals from even highly entangled covariates, unlocking counterfactual, "what-if," analyses. Applying
papers.summary: DeepDive is a deep-learning framework that disentangles the effects of individual biological factors from single-nucleus ATAC-seq data, addressing the problem of multicollinearity in human cohort studies. It accurately reconstructs chromatin accessibility, outperforms existing methods when covariate information is incomplete, and enables counterfactual 'what-if' analyses by recovering true biological signals from entangled covariates.

papers.title: OscillomeR infers ultradian oscillations and targets of the Hes family.
papers.abstract: The Hes family, basic-helix-loop-helix transcription factors and downstream effectors of Notch signaling, regulate the fate choices of pancreatic progenitors, muscle stem cells, neuronal progenitors, and presomitic mesoderm cells. Bioluminescence imaging (BLI) has revealed ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family members Hes1, Hes5, and Hes7. However, identifying which of the Hes target genes also oscillate remains challenging due to the time-consuming and costly nature of tracking individual target genes using BLI. Here, we propose OscillomeR, a computational framework that reconstructs u
papers.summary: OscillomeR is a computational framework that infers ultradian oscillatory dynamics of Hes-family transcription factors and predicts which of their downstream target genes also oscillate, bypassing the need for costly and time-consuming bioluminescence imaging of each gene individually. This provides a scalable approach to mapping the oscillatory gene network downstream of Notch signaling.

papers.title: Disagreement-informed arbitration for gene regulatory network inference: A score-level meta-classifier and a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflict.
papers.abstract: Gene regulatory network inference methods routinely disagree about individual edges, and practitioners resolve those conflicts by choosing one method or averaging them all. We ask whether the conflict can instead be arbitrated per edge. A gradient-boosted classifier is trained on the raw scores that ten inference methods-correlation-based, information-theoretic, sparse-regression and tree-ensemble, including GENIE3, GRNBoost2, CLR and ARACNe-assign to each candidate regulator-target pair, so that the weight given to each method varies from edge to edge. Across six single-cell perturbation scre
papers.summary: The authors propose a meta-classifier that arbitrates disagreements between ten gene regulatory network inference methods on a per-edge basis, using a gradient-boosted model trained on the raw scores each method assigns to candidate regulator-target pairs. This edge-specific weighting outperforms choosing a single method or averaging them, and the work also offers a diagnostic typology of inter-method conflicts. The approach is evaluated across six single-cell perturbation screens.

papers.title: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Data to Identify Lactylation-Related Gene Signatures in Hepatic Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
papers.abstract: Hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI) is not only a common complication of liver transplantation and major hepatic surgery but also a critical determinant of postoperative prognosis. Lactate metabolic reprogramming has been observed in HIRI, yet the role of lactate and its related lactylation in the pathogenesis of HIRI remains unclear. To address this, we integrated single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data with multiple bioinformatic approaches. Five single-cell gene set activity scoring methods (AUCell, UCell, singscore, ssGSEA, and AddModuleScore) were applied to evaluate lactylation activity
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA sequencing data to investigate lactylation-related gene signatures in hepatic ischemia-reperfusion injury (HIRI). Using multiple gene set activity scoring methods and machine learning algorithms, the authors identify lactylation-associated molecular patterns that may contribute to HIRI pathogenesis. The work highlights lactate metabolism reprogramming as a potentially important mechanism in liver injury following transplantation or surgery.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis reveals an epithelial cell-derived prognostic and immunotherapeutic signature with ADAM12 as a key functional regulator in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: This study developed a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for NSCLC using single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data. By integrating TCGA and GEO datasets with machine learning, we identified key epithelial cells-related genes predictive of immunotherapy response. PIS effectively stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS individuals showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. We confirmed the high expression of ADAM12 in both tissue samples and cell lines, and validated its functional roles through cellular assays. Furthermore, mouse model experiments d
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to build a Prognostic and Immunotherapeutic Signature (PIS) for non-small cell lung cancer, based on epithelial cell-related genes. The signature stratifies patients by survival and immune activity, with low-PIS patients showing better outcomes and higher immune infiltration. ADAM12 was validated as a highly expressed gene with functional roles in cellular and mouse model experiments.

papers.title: NEAT1 Coordinates a PDLIM5-CACNA1C Regulatory Program Associated with a Potentially Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyocyte State in the Border Zone During Early Myocardial Infarction.
papers.abstract: Patients with early-stage myocardial infarction (MI) are at high risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias, yet the cell-type-specific molecular landscape associated with post-infarction arrhythmogenesis has not been systematically characterized. This study integrates single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics to define a cardiomyocyte subpopulation in early MI and dissect the NEAT1-centered regulatory network driving its ion channel remodeling. Single-nucleus transcriptomic data from post-MI human hearts were re-analyzed to identify a distinct subpopulation, termed arrhythmia-potential cardio
papers.summary: This study integrates single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics to identify a distinct cardiomyocyte subpopulation in the border zone of early myocardial infarction that shows arrhythmogenic potential. The authors characterize a NEAT1-centered regulatory network involving PDLIM5 and CACNA1C that drives ion channel remodeling in this subpopulation, suggesting a mechanism linking early post-MI transcriptional changes to malignant ventricular arrhythmia risk.

papers.title: Deciphering the Genetic Underpinnings of Liver Cirrhosis-Heart Failure Comorbidity Through Multi-Omics: CRIM1 as a Key Endothelial Mediator.
papers.abstract: The co-occurrence of liver cirrhosis (LC) and heart failure (HF) poses considerable clinical challenges, yet the cellular and molecular determinants of this comorbidity remain poorly characterized. To address this, we developed an integrative multi-omics pipeline encompassing GWAS meta-analysis, gsMap-based spatial transcriptomic projection, GeneEnrich functional annotation, single-cell atlas construction, seismicGWAS and ECLIPSER cell-type scoring, eCAVIAR and fastenloc colocalization, hdWGCNA network inference, scTenifoldKnk in silico gene perturbation, and GCTA-COJO fine-mapping. Quality-co
papers.summary: This study integrates GWAS, spatial transcriptomics, single-cell atlases, and network inference to uncover shared genetic and cellular mechanisms linking liver cirrhosis and heart failure. The authors identify CRIM1 as a key endothelial mediator of this comorbidity, highlighting a vascular-endothelial axis that may connect the two diseases. The work demonstrates how multi-omics pipelines can prioritize causal genes and cell types for complex comorbid conditions.

papers.title: Machine learning identifies ac4C-related prognostic signature and TUBA1C as therapeutic target in COAD.
papers.abstract: To explore the role of N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes (acRGs) in colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and identify reliable prognostic biomarkers and potential therapeutic targets. Multi-source transcriptomic datasets (TCGA-COAD, GSE39582, GSE17536) and single-cell RNA-seq data were analyzed. Ten machine learning algorithms were integrated to construct an acRG-based prognostic signature (acRGBS). Immune microenvironment (TME) and genomic profiling were performed, with in vitro functional experiments validating TUBA1C's role. acRGBS, comprising four hub genes (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C), e
papers.journal: Mammalian genome : official journal of the International Mammalian Genome Society
papers.summary: This study used multi-source transcriptomic and single-cell RNA-seq data with ten machine learning algorithms to build a prognostic signature based on N4-acetylcytidine (ac4C)-related genes in colon adenocarcinoma. The four-gene signature (SARAF, CDC42SE2, TSPYL2, TUBA1C) stratified patients by prognosis and was linked to immune microenvironment and genomic features, with in vitro experiments supporting TUBA1C as a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: A High-Resolution Stereo-Seq Spatial Transcriptomic Resource for Adult Holstein Cattle Liver.
papers.abstract: The bovine liver is a highly compartmentalized organ that plays essential roles in continuous gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling; however, its spatial molecular architecture has remained largely uncharacterized due to the limitations of traditional bulk and single-cell approaches. To address this gap, Spatial Enhanced Resolution Omics-sequencing (Stereo-seq) was utilized to generate a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver, and a refined reference-guided workflow was implemented to overcome standard annotation limitations in livestock. Raw sequ
papers.summary: This study generated a subcellular-resolution (500 nm) spatial transcriptomic map of an adult Holstein cattle liver using Stereo-seq, providing the first detailed spatial molecular atlas of the bovine liver. The authors also developed a refined reference-guided workflow to improve gene annotation in livestock species where standard annotations are incomplete. The resource reveals the spatial organization of hepatic compartments and their roles in gluconeogenesis and nitrogen recycling.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and machine learning analysis identifies a tumor doubling time-related prognostic signature and therapeutic targets in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) exhibits marked molecular heterogeneity and diverse clinical outcomes, partly influenced by HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. Although tumor doubling time (TDT) reflects tumor growth kinetics and has prognostic relevance, its molecular basis in HNSCC remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing with machine learning to identify a gene signature associated with tumor doubling time (TDT) in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). The authors link this TDT-related signature to prognosis and potential therapeutic targets, while accounting for HPV status and the tumor immune microenvironment. The work suggests that tumor growth kinetics can be captured molecularly and used for patient stratification.

papers.title: A systematic benchmark of bioinformatics methods for single-cell and spatial RNA-seq nanopore long reads data.
papers.abstract: Alternative splicing plays a crucial role in transcriptomic complexity, yet remains difficult to resolve at the single-cell level due to the limitations of short-read technologies. Coupling single-cell with long-read sequencing offers full-length transcript coverage, enabling more accurate isoform detection. Diverse computational tools tailored for single-cell and spatial long-read transcriptomics have been developed. To compare the effectiveness of these approaches, we generated paired short-read and Nanopore long-read single-cell datasets, tailored for benchmarking bioinformatics tools. We e
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic benchmark of computational tools for analyzing single-cell and spatial RNA-seq data generated with Nanopore long-read sequencing. The authors generated paired short-read and long-read single-cell datasets to evaluate how well different bioinformatics methods detect full-length transcripts and alternative splicing isoforms. The study provides guidance on tool selection for researchers working with long-read single-cell and spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Interpretable multi-omics integration across mixed-order tensors with MANTRA.
papers.abstract: The integration of multi-modal molecular data is crucial for understanding complex diseases, but existing methods struggle with modern experimental designs that generate datasets with mixed-order tensors-for example, a third-order drug-response tensor alongside a second-order transcriptomics matrix. Here, we present MANTRA (Multi-view ANalysis with Tensor and matRix Alignment), a probabilistic framework that integrates collections of tensors of different orders, combining the strengths of group factor analysis and tensor decomposition. MANTRA learns interpretable latent factors and naturally h
papers.summary: MANTRA is a probabilistic framework that integrates multi-omics datasets with mixed-order tensors, such as third-order drug-response tensors alongside second-order transcriptomics matrices. It combines group factor analysis with tensor decomposition to learn interpretable latent factors, addressing a gap in existing integration methods for modern experimental designs.

papers.title: Alignment-free integration of single-nucleus ATAC-seq across species with sPYce.
papers.abstract: Changes in gene regulation largely contribute to differences in cellular identities and phenotypes between species. Single-nucleus assays for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (snATAC-seq) are an efficient strategy to identify putative gene regulatory elements and provide new insight into evolutionary divergence of regulatory programmes. However, no dedicated framework exists to integrate and compare snATAC-seq data across species, while methods designed for single-cell gene expression data have serious limitations. Here we present sPYce, a cross-species snATAC-seq integration m
papers.summary: The authors present sPYce, a new computational framework for integrating single-nucleus ATAC-seq data across different species without requiring sequence alignment. This addresses a gap in cross-species regulatory comparison, since existing single-cell integration tools designed for gene expression data perform poorly on chromatin accessibility data. sPYce enables direct comparison of gene regulatory programmes between species at single-cell resolution.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning and multimodal single cell analysis link NR4A2 to CD8+ T-cell terminal exhaustion and a CD8-adjusted prognostic signature in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Terminal exhaustion of CD8+ tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes constrains the benefit of immune-checkpoint blockade in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). The orphan nuclear receptor NR4A2 (Nurr1) belongs to a transcription-factor family implicated in murine T-cell exhaustion, yet its behaviour in the human HCC microenvironment has not been characterised across data modalities. We asked whether NR4A2 is specifically coupled to the terminal-exhaustion programme of human HCC CD8+ T cells, and whether that coupling is reflected in chromatin, tissue topography and bulk-tumour outcome data.
papers.summary: This study uses explainable machine learning combined with multimodal single-cell analysis to show that the transcription factor NR4A2 is specifically linked to terminal exhaustion of CD8+ T cells in hepatocellular carcinoma. The authors further develop a CD8-adjusted prognostic signature, suggesting NR4A2 and its associated exhaustion programme could serve as biomarkers or therapeutic targets for improving immunotherapy outcomes in HCC.

papers.title: Ten quick tips for spatial transcriptomics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) enables genome-wide gene expression profiling while retaining spatial context within tissue sections. Since the foundational work by Ståhl et al. in 2016, the field has expanded rapidly, with diverse platforms now spanning sequencing-based (e.g., Visium, Visium HD, Slide-seq, Stereo-seq, and Seq-Scope) and imaging-based (e.g., MERFISH, Xenium, and CosMx SMI) approaches. The breadth of platforms, data structures, and computational tools, however, can be daunting for newcomers. Here, we present ten quick tips spanning the entire ST research workflow: whether ST suits
papers.summary: This paper provides ten practical tips for researchers new to spatial transcriptomics, covering the full workflow from experimental design through data analysis. It addresses the rapidly expanding landscape of sequencing-based and imaging-based platforms, helping newcomers navigate platform choices and computational tools.

papers.title: Integrated Multi-Omics and Radiogenomic Analysis Identifies S100B and ITGB5 as Complementary Candidate Biomarkers of Glioblastoma Heterogeneity.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity, diffuse invasion, and a profoundly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. In this study, we applied an integrative multi-omics and radiogenomic framework to identify candidate biomarkers reflecting complementary dimensions of GBM heterogeneity. Public bulk transcriptomic datasets were integrated to define GBM-related differentially expressed genes, which were intersected with curated microbiota-associated gene sets as a hypothesis-generating screening strategy. Machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation were use
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomic data with radiogenomic and microbiota-associated gene sets to identify candidate glioblastoma biomarkers, nominating S100B and ITGB5 as complementary markers of tumor heterogeneity. Machine-learning models with SHAP interpretation were used to prioritize and interpret these candidates. The work is hypothesis-generating and relies on public datasets without experimental validation.

papers.title: AI-Assisted Multimodal Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Senescence-Related Prognostic Signature and Characterizes ADGRF5-Associated Malignant Phenotypes in Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence (CS) is increasingly recognized as an important cell-state programme involved in breast cancer progression and therapeutic response, but its context-dependent molecular heterogeneity limits its application in prognostic assessment. In this study, GeneCompass-based all-gene in silico perturbation analysis was performed to identify candidate genes predicted to induce senescence or rejuvenation, thereby expanding the known senescence-related gene set. Machine learning further established a seven-gene prognostic signature that may serve as an adjunctive tool for prognostic asse
papers.summary: This study used an AI model (GeneCompass) to perform in silico perturbation of all genes in breast cancer transcriptomic data, identifying new candidate genes that may induce or reverse cellular senescence. Machine learning then built a seven-gene senescence-related prognostic signature and linked ADGRF5 to malignant phenotypes, offering a potential adjunctive tool for breast cancer prognosis.

papers.title: Combined multi-omics profiling and machine learning analysis reveals that Bregs and RPS2 promote bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma.
papers.abstract: The bone is the primary site of distant metastasis in patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC), and bone metastasis (BM) significantly increases mortality. Deciphering the complex crosstalk between cancer cells and their tumor microenvironment (TME) is crucial for identifying therapeutic targets aimed at eliminating metastasis-initiating cells and preventing the establishment of overt metastases. Regulatory B cells (Bregs), a specialized B-cell subset endowed with potent immunosuppressive functions, play a pivotal regulatory role within the TME. However, their specific contributions, pheno
papers.summary: This study combines multi-omics profiling with machine learning to investigate how regulatory B cells (Bregs) and the gene RPS2 contribute to bone metastasis in nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The authors identify these factors as potential drivers of the metastatic process, suggesting they could serve as therapeutic targets to prevent bone metastasis in NPC patients.

papers.title: STC1 is associated with tumor progression and suppressive niches in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) exhibits high recurrence and therapy resistance. We aimed to investigate the undefined role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in LSCC pathogenesis.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of Stanniocalcin-1 (STC1) in laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC), a cancer with high recurrence and therapy resistance. The authors associate STC1 expression with tumor progression and the formation of immunosuppressive niches, suggesting it may contribute to LSCC pathogenesis. The findings point to STC1 as a potential biomarker or therapeutic target in this cancer type.

papers.title: Integration of Spatial Transcriptomics and Mendelian Randomization Identifies Candidate Molecular Regulators of Endometrial Cancer Progression.
papers.abstract: Endometrial cancer (EC) is a common gynecologic malignancy arising from the epithelial cells of the endometrium. The marked cellular heterogeneity of EC and features of its tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) contribute to disease complexity and have been associated with poor prognosis. This study integrates single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify candidate genes associated with EC. Single-cell analysis identified MM0 as a putative stemness-associated transcriptional subpopulation with the highest CytoTRACE-inferred score; irGSEA indic
papers.summary: This study combines single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and Mendelian randomization to identify candidate genes involved in endometrial cancer progression. The authors pinpoint a stemness-associated macrophage subpopulation (MM0) and use genetic causal inference to prioritize molecular regulators linked to the tumor immune microenvironment.

papers.title: The Dual Face of Gingival Mesenchymal Stem Cell Paracrine Signalling in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Pro-Tumour Transcriptional Programme and a Hypothesis-Generating Drug-Repurposing Screen.
papers.abstract: Background: In our companion study, the gingival mesenchymal stem cell (GMSC) secretome suppresses oxidative stress and induces apoptosis in primary oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, where those wet-lab results are themselves reported as preliminary; here we ask whether it also engages a proliferation × migration programme in patient tissue. The two arms differ in read-out type (apoptosis and redox there, transcript abundance here), not in opposed function. Methods: Primary OSCC cells received GMSC-conditioned medium (GMSC-CM) or indirect Transwell co-culture, assayed by RT-qPCR (VEGF
papers.summary: This study examines how paracrine signals from gingival mesenchymal stem cells (GMSCs) affect oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) cells, finding that GMSC-conditioned medium induces a pro-tumour transcriptional programme linked to proliferation and migration in patient tissue. The authors also perform a hypothesis-generating drug-repurposing screen to identify compounds that might counteract these effects. The work highlights the dual, context-dependent nature of GMSC paracrine signalling in cancer.

papers.title: Particulate Matter Exposure and Diabetic Kidney Dysfunction: Insights from Integrated Transcriptomic and Bioinformatics Analyses.
papers.abstract: Exposure to ambient particulate matter (PM) has been linked to renal dysfunction, particularly in diabetic populations, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We performed bidirectional Mendelian randomization to assess causal relationships between PM exposure and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), integrated transcriptomic datasets to identify PM-related genes overlapping with diabetic kidney disease (DKD) differentially expressed genes, and applied machine learning approaches to select key feature genes and construct diagnostic models. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic
papers.summary: This study combines Mendelian randomization, transcriptomic integration, and machine learning to investigate how particulate matter exposure contributes to diabetic kidney dysfunction. The authors identify shared genes between PM exposure and diabetic kidney disease, and use single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to build diagnostic models highlighting key feature genes.

papers.title: Pseudotime-conditioned diffusion models for imputing time-series single-cell data.
papers.abstract: Probabilistic diffusion-based imputation methods have demonstrated superior performance over many state-of-the-art approaches for imputing single-cell data. However, existing methods typically rely on isotropic Gaussian noise and canonical observation time, limiting their ability to capture structured temporal dependencies and continuous cellular dynamics. In time-series single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data, these limitations are exacerbated by the small number of experimentally measured time points and the substantial heterogeneity among cells collected at the same time point, causing observe
papers.summary: The paper introduces pseudotime-conditioned diffusion models for imputing time-series single-cell RNA-seq data. By conditioning on pseudotime rather than canonical observation times and using structured noise, the method better captures continuous cellular dynamics and temporal dependencies. This addresses key limitations of existing diffusion-based imputation methods, especially when few time points are available and cells are heterogeneous.

papers.title: Multi-omics and machine learning reveal LYZ and ISG15 as diagnostic and therapeutic targets in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease.
papers.abstract: CKD represents a substantial worldwide health challenge, defined by the gradual development of tubulointerstitial fibrosis and reduced renal performance. Autoimmune-mediated factors are central to this pathological process, yet early diagnostic biomarkers and specific therapeutic targets are scarce. The objective of this research is to systematically pinpoint crucial specific genes that contribute to autoimmune-mediated CKD progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with machine learning to identify LYZ and ISG15 as key genes involved in autoimmune-mediated chronic kidney disease. These genes are proposed as potential diagnostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets, addressing the current lack of early detection markers and specific treatments for this condition.

papers.title: Identification and Validation of a Two-Gene NK Cell-Related Risk Model for COPD: Integration of Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Analysis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) involves chronic inflammation with potential involvement of natural killer (NK) cells, but NK cell-related diagnostic markers remain limited. This study aimed to identify NK cell-related hub genes and construct a risk model for COPD.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data to identify NK cell-related hub genes and build a two-gene risk model for COPD. The model is validated as a potential diagnostic tool, highlighting NK cell involvement in COPD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Progress and challenges in exploring the pathogenesis of depressive disorders via RNA sequencing.
papers.abstract: Depressive disorders (DD) are highly heterogeneous psychiatric illnesses. Their complex pathogenesis, coupled with suboptimal response rates to current clinical treatments, poses significant challenges to global mental health. High-throughput RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has emerged as a powerful tool for dissecting the molecular mechanisms of DD at the transcriptomic level. This paper reviews recent advances utilizing bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq), and single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) to explore the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), perinatal depression (PND), per
papers.summary: This review surveys how bulk, single-cell, and single-nucleus RNA sequencing have been applied to dissect the molecular pathogenesis of depressive disorders, including major depressive disorder and perinatal depression. It highlights both the insights gained into transcriptomic dysregulation and the ongoing challenges in translating these findings into clinical utility.

papers.title: Single-cell Raman profiling of B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation with transcriptome inference.
papers.abstract: Label-free profiling of cellular transcriptional and metabolic states during B cell differentiation and malignant transformation remains technically challenging. Raman spectroscopy offers a non-destructive alternative for single-cell biochemical characterization, yet its ability to infer transcriptomic profiles and distinguish leukemic cells has been limited.
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell Raman spectroscopy to profile B cell differentiation and leukemic transformation without labels, aiming to infer transcriptomic states from biochemical signatures. It demonstrates that Raman spectral features can distinguish leukemic cells from normal differentiating B cells, offering a non-destructive alternative to conventional transcriptomic profiling.

papers.title: From transcriptomic profiling to precision oncology: a bibliometric analysis of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia.
papers.abstract: RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) has become an important tool for investigating the molecular heterogeneity of acute myeloid leukemia (AML); however, the global development and thematic evolution of this field remain inadequately characterized.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the global research landscape of RNA sequencing in acute myeloid leukemia, examining publication trends, key contributors, and thematic evolution over time. It aims to characterize how transcriptomic profiling has progressed toward precision oncology applications in AML.

papers.title: Peripheral blood cells and immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis: a retrospective clinical study with pharmacovigilance and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated myocarditis (ICI-M) is a rare but potentially lethal immune-related adverse event (irAE). Early identification of fulminant (severe) cases remains challenging, and the peripheral immune derangements underlying ICI-M are incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This retrospective clinical study investigates immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated myocarditis (ICI-M), a rare but potentially fatal side effect of cancer immunotherapy, using pharmacovigilance data and single-cell analysis of peripheral blood cells. The authors aim to identify peripheral immune signatures that could help distinguish fulminant (severe) cases early and better characterize the immune derangements underlying this condition.

papers.title: An hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model exhibiting proximal-distal epithelial features for modeling pulmonary fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and irreversible interstitial lung disease with limited therapeutic options. Existing hiPSC-derived lung organoid models are largely restricted to single epithelial lineages and cannot endogenously integrate multiple pulmonary cell types, limiting mechanistic studies and drug screening.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: The authors developed a hiPSC-derived multi-lineage lung model that captures both proximal and distal epithelial features, overcoming the single-lineage limitation of prior lung organoid systems. This model enables more physiologically relevant studies of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and drug screening by integrating multiple pulmonary cell types endogenously.

papers.title: Multi-omics mapping of PSC genetic risk to a high TWAS-active JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program: bridging single-cell heterogeneity, spatial fibrotic niches, and machine learning selection.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease with progressive peribiliary inflammation and fibrosis. Disease-modifying therapies are lacking, and the cell-type-specific mechanisms linking genetic susceptibility to pathogenic immune states remain incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to map primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) genetic risk variants to a specific JAML+ lipid-associated macrophage program that shows high transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) activity. The authors combine single-cell heterogeneity analysis, spatial profiling of fibrotic niches, and machine learning to link genetic susceptibility to this pathogenic immune cell state.

papers.title: A parallel convolution attention network for crop genomic prediction.
papers.abstract: Genome prediction is a breeding strategy that predicts crop phenotype through genomic markers. Traditional statistical models cannot accurately capture the complex relationships between genotypes and phenotypes, and deep neural networks have shown significant advantages in capturing nonlinear relationships. Deep learning methods in genome selection primarily utilize sequential convolutional kernels, which can lead to challenges such as gradient disappearance and computational inefficiency. In this study a novel crop genomic prediction method based on a parallel convolutional attention network
papers.summary: The authors propose a parallel convolution attention network for genomic prediction in crops, aiming to better capture nonlinear genotype-phenotype relationships than traditional statistical models and sequential convolutional deep learning approaches. The parallel convolutional design is intended to mitigate gradient vanishing and improve computational efficiency in genome selection.

papers.title: Engineered Exosomal miRNAs for Post-Stroke Neural Repair: Mechanisms, Delivery Strategies, and Translational Challenges.
papers.abstract: Functional neurological recovery after ischemic stroke remains a formidable challenge in neuroscience. Exosomes serve as pivotal mediators of intercellular communication, and the microRNAs (miRNAs) they carry, in particular, offer a promising "cell-free therapy" strategy for promoting neurological repair. This review systematically summarizes the multi-target mechanisms by which exosomal miRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit (NVU) and outlines technical strategies to enhance exosomal therapeutic efficacy through targeted modification and engineered cargo loading, with the aim of constructing
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how exosomal microRNAs regulate the neurovascular unit after ischemic stroke and can be harnessed as a cell-free therapy for neural repair. It also surveys engineering strategies—targeted modification and cargo loading—to improve exosome delivery and efficacy, while outlining translational barriers.

papers.title: Spatial multi-omics decoding of the fracture nonunion niche: from immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk to precision regeneration.
papers.abstract: Fracture nonunion - the failure of bone to heal without surgical intervention - affects 5%-10% of all fractures and represents a substantial clinical and economic burden. Despite decades of research, the cellular and molecular mechanisms that distinguish successful repair from nonunion remain incompletely understood, largely because the fracture niche is a spatially organized, multicellular ecosystem whose crosstalk cannot be captured by bulk analyses. The recent convergence of spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics, and computational integration methods has opene
papers.summary: This review discusses how spatial multi-omics technologies (spatial transcriptomics, single-cell multi-omics, spatial proteomics) can decode the cellular and molecular ecosystem of fracture nonunion, a condition affecting 5-10% of fractures. It highlights immune-vascular-skeletal crosstalk within the spatially organized fracture niche and proposes these approaches as a path toward precision regenerative medicine.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell analysis characterizes malignant epithelial programs and context-dependent immune associations of MP7/SERINC2 in colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) comprises heterogeneous malignant epithelial states, but it remains unclear which transcriptional programs recur across patients and how these programs relate to the immune context.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated single-cell analysis to identify recurrent malignant epithelial transcriptional programs in colorectal cancer and examines how these programs associate with immune context. It specifically highlights MP7/SERINC2 as a context-dependent marker linking malignant cell states to immune associations.

papers.title: Spatially resolved gene expression analysis illuminates location-specific functions in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta.
papers.abstract: Reef-building coral polyps contain multiple specialized tissue types with distinct functions, from feeding and defense to symbiosis and skeleton formation. While these cell types have been characterized microscopically and more recently via single-cell RNA sequencing, spatially resolved high-throughput gene expression profiling remains limited in corals. Here we combine Laser Capture Microdissection with RNA sequencing to characterize tissue-specific gene expression in the reef building coral Pocillopora acuta. Oral tissues, adjacent to the seawater, exhibited 1,253 upregulated genes enriched
papers.summary: This study uses laser capture microdissection combined with RNA sequencing to profile tissue-specific gene expression in the reef-building coral Pocillopora acuta. The authors identify distinct transcriptional signatures for different tissue regions, with oral tissues showing 1,253 upregulated genes enriched for functions related to their interface with seawater. This provides a spatially resolved view of coral tissue specialization that complements existing single-cell approaches.

papers.title: Network-informed deconvolution of bulk immune gene co-expression reveals single-cell programs and spatial organization.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has opened unprecedented possibilities to explore the complexity of the immune system. However, existing methods primarily rely on expression-based clustering analysis, which lacks mechanistic explanations for immune cell states and encounters challenges in integrating multi-scale data.
papers.summary: This paper introduces a network-informed deconvolution approach that uses immune gene co-expression networks to extract single-cell programs from bulk RNA-seq data, linking them to spatial organization. The method aims to overcome the limitations of expression-based clustering by providing mechanistic interpretations of immune cell states and enabling multi-scale data integration.

papers.title: Spatial compartmentalization of melanoma cell states reveals CAF-associated tumor cells with enhanced proliferative capacity.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key components of the melanoma tumor microenvironment and have been implicated in immune evasion and therapy resistance. However, the spatial relationships between CAFs, extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, and immune exclusion remain incompletely characterized.
papers.summary: This study uses spatial profiling to map how cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) organize the melanoma tumor microenvironment, revealing that CAFs associate with specific tumor cell states that have enhanced proliferative capacity. The work links CAF proximity to ECM remodeling and immune exclusion, suggesting spatial compartmentalization shapes tumor behavior.

papers.title: Integrated Pan-Cancer, Single-Cell, and Spatial Transcriptomic Analyses Identify ZDHHC12 as a Biomarker Associated with Macrophage Infiltration and the Immune Landscape in Glioma.
papers.abstract: The tumor immune microenvironment (TME) critically influences cancer progression and therapeutic response. However, the pan-cancer expression landscape, prognostic relevance, and spatial distribution of ZDHHC12 remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated the prognostic value of ZDHHC12 and its associations with immune microenvironmental features and drug sensitivity.
papers.summary: This study integrates pan-cancer, single-cell, and spatial transcriptomic data to characterize ZDHHC12, identifying it as a biomarker linked to macrophage infiltration and the immune landscape in glioma. The authors also examine its prognostic value and associations with immune microenvironmental features and drug sensitivity.

papers.title: Shared genetic architecture of smoking dependence and Crohn's disease: A cross-trait analysis of GWAS summary statistics.
papers.abstract: Smoking dependence (SD) and Crohn's disease (CD) are epidemiologically associated, but whether this relationship reflects shared genetic susceptibility remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses cross-trait analysis of GWAS summary statistics to investigate whether smoking dependence and Crohn's disease share a genetic basis, motivated by their known epidemiological association. The authors aim to determine if the relationship between these traits reflects shared genetic susceptibility rather than purely environmental or confounding effects.
